children.content: ceradoc-docx reads Microsoft Word .docx files via Uniword and transforms the OOXML model tree into Ceradoc's canonical CoreModel. Once in CoreModel, the document can be serialized to AsciiDoc, Markdown, or any other supported output format.

children.content: The gem depends on ceradoc and uniword, which will be installed automatically.
lines: The gem depends on ceradoc and uniword, which will be installed automatically.

children.content:
require 'ceradoc'
require 'ceradoc/docx'
adoc = Ceradoc.convert("input.docx", from: :docx, to: :asciidoc)

core = Ceradoc.parse("input.docx", format: :docx)
core.title         # => "Document Title"
core.children      # => Array of sections, paragraphs, tables, etc.
# Serialize to any format
adoc = Ceradoc.serialize(core, to: :asciidoc)
html = Ceradoc.serialize(core, to: :html)
lines: core.children      # => Array of sections, paragraphs, tables, etc.

children.content:
# Convert DOCX to AsciiDoc
ceradoc convert document.docx -o output.adoc
# Convert DOCX to Markdown
ceradoc convert document.docx -o output.md

children.content:
DOCX file
  → Uniword::DocumentFactory.from_file
  → OOXML model tree (Uniword::Wordprocessingml::*)
  → Ceradoc::Docx::Transform::ToCoreModel (rule-based dispatch)
  → CoreModel tree (canonical hub)
  → FromCoreModel (AsciiDoc or Markdown)
  → Format model tree → Serializer → .adoc or .md file
lines: → Format model tree → Serializer → .adoc or .md file

children.content: The transform uses a rule registry with priority-based dispatch. Each OOXML element type has a dedicated rule class that produces a typed CoreModel node. Style-based semantic detection (headings, lists, quotes) is handled by StyleResolver and NumberingResolver.
